newsitem.title: JAPAN: Three Japanese rangers die, volcanic gas suspected.
newsitem.headline: Three Japanese rangers die, volcanic gas suspected.

text.p: Three members of Japan's Self-Defence Force died and 18 others became ill, apparently poisoned by gas from a nearby volcanic hot spring during a training exercise in northern Japan, a military spokesman said on Sunday.
"We believe the three rangers may have died after inhaling a gas coming from a hot spring. In all 21 rangers lost consciousness or got sick," he said.
The 23-man Ground Self-Defence Force ranger unit was on a two-day hike in forests on Hakkoda mountain on the northern tip of the main island of Honshu, around 600 km (400 miles) northeast of Tokyo.
The spokesman said that several of the group collapsed near a volcanic pond at around 8 p.m. (1100 GMT) on Saturday.
"When others went to rescue them they fell unconscious or found it difficult to breathe and move. But some of the group managed to radio for help," he added.
"The three were reported dead by hospital officials at around midnight."
The rangers were all carrying gas masks as part of their kit, he said.
"But gas masks sometimes don't work against volcanic gases," he added.
The area is known for its hot springs and sporadic leaks of poisonous gas, with cows having fallen unconscious in previous incidents.
All Ground Self-Defence Force training exercises were suspended while officials probed the cause of the incident, the spokesman said.
Nine rangers were still receiving treatment in hospital but their condition was stable, he added.
